lines.japanese: パルクレープをあとにした俺は、さっそくメモにある次の場所へ向かっていた。
lines.english: After leaving Paru Crêpes, I set off at once for the next place on my note.

lines.japanese: グローヴ街のとば口にある、メダルコーナーに特化した中規模のゲームセンター。数日前、そこの店先に背もたれ付きの赤いチャリが停まってたって言う話。
lines.english: A midsized arcade at the entrance to Grove Street, specializing in medal games. A few days ago, somebody had supposedly seen a red bicycle with a backrest parked outside.

lines.japanese: ゲーセンだから閉店はたぶん１２時だろう。現在、閉店一時間前。蛍の光にはまだちょっと早い。よっぽどちんたら歩かないかぎりヨユーで間に合うだろう。
lines.english: It was an arcade, so closing time was probably midnight. It was eleven now—a little early for the closing-time “Auld Lang Syne.” Unless we dawdled spectacularly, we’d make it with time to spare.

lines.japanese: っつうことで、ま、それはいいんだけど──
lines.english: So that was all fine and good, except—

lines.japanese: 「──なんでおまえが付いてきてんの」
lines.english: “—why are you following me?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、今日ぐらいいいじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “Oh, surely just for today is all right.”

lines.japanese: 「なに今日ぐらいって。なんで今日はいいんだよ」
lines.english: “What's ‘just for today’ mean? Why is today all right?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃー、付いてっちゃいけないんですかー」
lines.english: “Then am I not allowed to come with you?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いけなくはねーけどさ。だって意味ないじゃん、二人で同じとこ探したって」
lines.english: “I didn't say you weren't allowed. It's just pointless for both of us to search the same place.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないですよー。一人より二人のほうが楽しいですよー」
lines.english: “Not at all. Two people have more fun than one.”

lines.japanese: 「だめじゃん」
lines.english: “That defeats the purpose.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでですかー。私いない方のが楽しいんですかー」
lines.english: “Why? Do you have more fun when I'm not there?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、そうじゃなくてさ。楽しい楽しくないは作業効率に関係ねーじゃん」
lines.english: “That's not what I mean. Fun or no fun has nothing to do with search efficiency.”

lines.japanese: 「ありますよー。楽しくないと飽きたりだれたりして、集中力の低下を招きますよー」
lines.english: “Of course it does. If it isn't fun, you get bored and sluggish, and then your concentration suffers.”

lines.japanese: こざかしいことを言うやつだ。
lines.english: What a crafty little thing.

lines.japanese: 「それにー、私の自転車を探すのに隼人さんばかり走りまわっていただくのも気がひけますしー」
lines.english: “Besides, I’d feel bad making you do all the running around when it’s my bicycle we’re looking for, Hayato, sir.”

lines.japanese: 慎ましいことも言うやつだ。
lines.english: What a modest little thing, too.

lines.japanese: 「……まあ、べつに俺はどっちでもいいけど」
lines.english: “...Well, I don't care either way.”

lines.japanese: 「どっちでもいいじゃありません。鳴さんと一緒の方が楽しいなと言いなさい」
lines.english: “Don’t say you don’t care. Say, ‘I have more fun with Naru.’”

lines.japanese: 図々しいことも言うやつだ。
lines.english: What a brazen little thing, too.

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: I raked at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそれで」
lines.english: “Fine. That, then.”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、あの、鳴さんと一緒の方が楽しいなってことですか？」
lines.english: “Wh... Um. You mean you *do* have more fun when Naru is with you?”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな。だから、そうだっつってんだろ」
lines.english: “Quit pestering me. Yeah, that's what I said.”

lines.japanese: 「もはっ！」
lines.english: “Mohah!”

lines.japanese: やつは奇怪なうめきをあげて、ブレザーの校章を握りつぶすように掴んだ。
lines.english: She emitted a bizarre moan and clutched the crest on her blazer as though crushing it in her fist.

lines.japanese: 「ううう、隼人さん……あ、あなた最近ちょっと、恋する乙女のここを刺激しすぎですよ」
lines.english: “Ooooh, Hayato… Lately you—you've been stimulating a maiden in love right here far too much.”

lines.japanese: 「どこだよ。乳首か」
lines.english: “Where, your nipple?”

lines.japanese: 「ぱかものー！」
lines.english: “You imbecile!”

lines.japanese: ひっぱたかれた。ジャンピングからの脳天はたき落としだった。
lines.english: She smacked me: a leaping hammer blow straight down onto the crown of my head.

lines.japanese: 「ってえな、なんだよ。おまえが『楽しい』言えっつったんじゃねーか。言わせといて逆ギレかよ」
lines.english: “Ow! What the hell? You're the one who told me to say I was having fun. You make me say it, then get mad at me?”

lines.japanese: 「やー、もー、あれですかねー。いよいよライバル登場して、私の恋も起承転結の『転』に差しかかってるんですかねー」
lines.english: “Oh dear. Has my rival finally appeared? Has my romance finally reached its big twist?”

lines.japanese: 「え、うそ。『起』とか『承』いつあったの」
lines.english: “Wait, seriously? When did we get the setup and buildup?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そーだあのー、亜衣ちゃんって前からあーなんですかー？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Has Ai always been like that?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　亜衣？　なに、いきなり」
lines.english: “Huh? Ai? Where'd that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、いまちゃんと流れに沿ってましたよう」
lines.english: “I was following the thread perfectly.”
“...Oh. Were you?”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、なんていうか私ー、彼女、もっと話しにくいひとだと思ってたんでー」
lines.english: “I suppose... I'd imagined she'd be much harder to talk to.”

lines.japanese: 「え、あいつ、教室ではカンジ違うの」
lines.english: “What, she acts different in class?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、どうなんでしょー。そもそも、ほとんど絡んだことなかったんで分からないんですけどー」
lines.english: “I wonder. We'd hardly ever interacted before, so I couldn't really say.”

lines.japanese: 「分かんないのに、話しにくそうだと思ってたの」
lines.english: “You thought she looked hard to talk to when you didn't even know?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、えー、そーですねー」
lines.english: “Well... yes, I suppose I did.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: まあ、そういうこともあるか。
lines.english: Well, I supposed that kind of thing happened.

lines.japanese: つーか、そういうことだらけか、世の中なんて。
lines.english: Hell, perhaps the whole world was made of that.

lines.japanese: 「でも、わりと普通に話してたじゃん。きのう」
lines.english: “But you two talked pretty normally yesterday.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、そうなんですよねー。自分でも意外というか不思議というかなんですけどー」
lines.english: “Yes. That's true. Even I was surprised. Or puzzled, perhaps.”

lines.japanese: 「なんか最近ー、前よりちょっと、ひとと話すのが滑らかになってきた気がするんですよー」
lines.english: “Lately, I feel as though I’ve gotten a little smoother at talking to people.”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「それ言ったら俺もアレだ、社交的？　社交的になっちゃった気はする」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, same here. Sociable—is that the word? Feels like I've gone and become sociable.”

lines.japanese: 「あらー、それは結構なことですねー」
lines.english: “My. That sounds like an excellent thing.”

lines.japanese: 「あぁ？　どうだかなあ。そんな、べつに、いいことずくめでもねーだろうけど」
lines.english: “Does it? I don’t know. It’s not all upside.”

lines.japanese: ひとりの方が気楽なことは多い。
lines.english: A lot of the time, being alone was easier.

lines.japanese: 少なくとも、ついこの前までの俺は、そう結論付けて生きてきたはずだ。
lines.english: At least, until very recently, that was the conclusion I'd lived by.

lines.japanese: 他人の顔色を窺って、媚びて怖れて相手を立てて、そうやって辛うじて輪の中に自分の居場所を確保したとしても──
lines.english: You watched every flicker in other people’s faces, flattered them, feared them, deferred to them, and through all that barely scraped out a place for yourself inside the circle—

lines.japanese: ──それでも些細な失敗や不運が起これば、すぐに天秤は引っくりかえる。
lines.english: —yet the smallest mistake or stroke of bad luck could tip the scales in an instant.

lines.japanese: だったら最初から居場所なんてない方が、どんなに安らかなことだろう。
lines.english: If that was how it worked, wouldn’t it be far more peaceful to have no place in it from the start?

lines.japanese: だから俺はつねづね鷲介のことを、馬鹿だ馬鹿だすっげえ馬鹿だと思っていた。
lines.english: That was why I'd always thought Shusuke an idiot. An idiot, an idiot, a monumental idiot.

lines.japanese: でもいま、俺はあの馬鹿をほんの少しだけ見直していた。かもしれない。いや、ほんのちょっとだけな。
lines.english: But now, maybe—just maybe—I thought a tiny bit better of that idiot. Only a tiny bit, mind you.

lines.japanese: そう、だから──
lines.english: So, yes—

lines.japanese: そのほんのちょっとの分だけ、俺の築いてきた人生観にプラスしてみようかな、とか。
lines.english: Maybe I could add that tiny concession to the view of life I’d built for myself.

lines.japanese: そんな風に思うんだ。
lines.english: That was what I found myself thinking.

lines.japanese: それでまたいつか痛い目を見ることもあるだろうけど、そんときはそんときだ、そんときになったらなんとかしよう。だって、もともとひとりには慣れてるんだから。
lines.english: Maybe it would get me hurt again someday. I’d deal with that when it happened. I was used to being alone anyway.

lines.japanese: っていうカンジでどうかな。
lines.english: How about that?

lines.japanese: 「えー、でもそうなると、いよいよ私ぴんちー？」
lines.english: “Oh—but if that's true, is poor Naru finally in trouble?”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、隼人さん。ものの本によると、誰にでも優しい男はときとして存在そのものが罪だそうですよ」
lines.english: “Hayato, according to certain books, a man who is kind to every woman sometimes commits a crime merely by existing.”

lines.japanese: 「なんの話だよ」
lines.english: “What the hell are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「だって亜衣ちゃん、いざとなったら押したおしそうだしー。そうなったら隼人さんもその場の雰囲気に流されそうだしー」
lines.english: “Ai seems like she'd pin you down the moment she got the chance. And then you'd probably just let the mood carry you away.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい女。本人の前でそういう失礼なこと言うんじゃねーよ。この場の雰囲気に流されてブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, woman. Don't say rude shit like that to a man's face. Keep it up and I'll let the mood carry me away—I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやー、これは鳴さん油断なりませんよー。敵は手ごわいですよー」
lines.english: “Oh no—Naru can't afford to let her guard down. The enemy is formidable.”

lines.japanese: 「手ごわいとかじゃねーよ。つか、だってアレだぜ。あいつ、亜衣って、彼氏いんぜ」
lines.english: “It ain't about her being formidable. Besides, you know… Ai's already got a boyfriend.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、まだ正式に付きあってはいないらしいけど、かなりそれに近いレベルの……ほら、おまえ知ってんだよな、おまえの兄貴んとこの、森里っつうクソ生意気な」
lines.english: “Well, sounds like they ain't officially dating yet, but they're damn close. You know him, right? That mouthy little bastard who hangs around your brother—Morisato?”

lines.japanese: 「あーあー、森里さん。あの髪の長い」
lines.english: “Oh, Morisato. The one with the long hair.”

lines.japanese: 「そーそー、森里さん。あの髪のうざい」
lines.english: “Yeah, Morisato. The one with the obnoxious hair.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　え！　亜衣ちゃんと森里さんがらぶらぶなんですか！」
lines.english: “What? What! Ai and Morisato are madly in love?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからビミョーなんだけど、まあ見たトコわりとそんな感じ？」
lines.english: “Like I said, it's a little vague, but from what I saw? More or less.”

lines.japanese: 「まじですか！　にゃんにゃんしてるんですか！」
lines.english: “Seriously? Are they sleeping together?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、にゃんにゃんはしてないみたいだけど、ちゅっちゅぐらいはしてんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Dunno about sleeping together, but they're probably kissing, at least.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、なるほどー、言うなればいまの私たちと同じぐらいな関係ということですね」
lines.english: “Ah, I see. In other words, their relationship is about where ours is now.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、違うだろ」
lines.english: “No, it isn’t.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだー、じゃあ亜衣ちゃんの隼人君好き好き光線は、ちょっと愉快なコミュニケーションだったんだー」
lines.english: “Oh. Then Ai's ‘I love Hayato’ beam was merely a slightly eccentric form of communication.”

lines.japanese: 「あーそそ、いつものこと。ま、ちょっとウゼぇけどさ、あいつ、おもしれーやつだよな」
lines.english: “Yeah, exactly. That's just how she always is. A little annoying, maybe, but she's a funny girl.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、もー私、亜衣ちゃん大好きですー」
lines.english: “Yes. I absolutely adore Ai now.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、一時はどうなるかと思いましたー」
lines.english: “My, and for a moment I was so worried about what might happen.”

lines.japanese: 「なに心配してんだよ、おまえは」
lines.english: “What were you so worried about?”

lines.japanese: 俺は鳴のデコを叩いた。
lines.english: I flicked Naru on the forehead.

lines.japanese: 「他の女になんか興味ねえよ。自信なさすぎじゃね」
lines.english: “I ain't interested in any other girls. You've got way too little confidence in yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「はうっ！」
lines.english: “Hau!”

lines.japanese: デコを叩いたのに、やつは何故かまた苦しげに乳首を握りつぶしていた。
lines.english: I had struck her forehead, yet for some reason she was once again gripping one nipple in apparent agony.

lines.japanese: 「む、胸が高鳴る……」
lines.english: “My… my heart is beating so fast…”

lines.japanese: グローヴ街入口アーチをくぐって十数歩のゲームセンター。
lines.english: The arcade stood barely a dozen paces beyond the arch at the entrance to Grove Street.

lines.japanese: コンビニの情報誌じゃアミューズメントパークとか呼ばれてるけど、俺に言わせりゃゲーセンはゲーセンだ。
lines.english: The convenience-store listings might call it an amusement park, but an arcade was an arcade as far as I was concerned.

lines.japanese: ゲーセンの入口からは、立ちならぶクレーンゲームが窺える。でも俺たちはもちろん自動ドアを通らず、建物の周辺を見まわした。
lines.english: Rows of crane games were visible through the entrance. Naturally, we ignored the automatic doors and searched around the outside instead.

lines.japanese: 結果はまあ、悪い意味での予想通り──
lines.english: The result was exactly what we'd expected, in the least desirable sense—

lines.japanese: 「ないですねー」
lines.english: “It isn't here.”

lines.japanese: 「だな」
lines.english: “Nope.”

lines.japanese: しかし諦めきれないのか、単に落ちつかないのか、鳴はいつまでも金を落とした子供みたいにきょろきょろ視線をさまよわせていた。
lines.english: Whether she couldn’t give up or simply couldn’t settle down, Naru kept looking around like a child who’d dropped some money.

lines.japanese: だから、なんとなく、早く次の場所へ移ろうとは言いだしづらかった。
lines.english: That somehow made it hard to suggest hurrying on to the next place.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、じゃあ念のため、おまえ──」
lines.english: “Hey. Just to be sure, why don't you—”

lines.japanese: 俺は人差し指で大きく円を描いた。
lines.english: I drew a broad circle with my index finger.

lines.japanese: 「──そっちからグルッと周ってきて。俺こっちから周る。だいたい五分後ぐらいにここ集合」
lines.english: “—go around that way. I'll circle from this side. Meet back here in about five minutes.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はいー、分かりましたー」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes. Got it.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は首を左右に振りながらとぼとぼ歩きだした。俺はそれを数歩分見送ってから振りかえり、やや速足で移動しはじめた。
lines.english: Naru trudged off, turning her head from side to side. I watched her for several paces, then turned and picked up my own pace.

lines.japanese: アルバトロスの裏を走る、さほど広くない辻に入った。
lines.english: I turned onto a narrow side street running behind the Albatross.

lines.japanese: お好み焼き屋とクイックマッサージの店のあいだ、外階段前の薄暗いくぼみに、顔の下半分を濃い髭で隠した中東系の外国人が立っていた。
lines.english: In a dim recess before an outdoor staircase, between an okonomiyaki shop and a quick-massage shop, stood a Middle Eastern man whose dense beard hid the lower half of his face.

lines.japanese: 男は片手に携帯電話を握り、キャッチでもビラ配りでもないくせに、道ゆくひとびとの波を油断のない黒目で掻きわけている。
lines.english: He held a cell phone in one hand. Neither touting nor passing out flyers, he nevertheless combed the stream of passersby with watchful dark eyes.

lines.japanese: 近年グローヴ街の至るところに高精度の監視カメラが設置されたせいで、一時期は完全に掃討されたけれど、最近たまにカメラの死角を見つけてはこういう輩が戻ってきてたりする。
lines.english: High-resolution security cameras had been installed throughout Grove Street in recent years, and for a time they had swept people like him away completely. Lately, though, they had begun finding the blind spots and creeping back.

lines.japanese: だから、俺たち通行人がきょろきょろと通りの端々に目を配りながら歩いていると──それでもって、もの欲しげな視線が偶然ぶつかったりしてしまうと、やつらはにこにこ愛想よく笑いながら近寄ってくる。
lines.english: So if you walked along peering into every corner of the street—and your searching gaze happened to meet one of theirs—they approached with broad, friendly smiles.

lines.japanese: 「ハイおにいさん！　なに探してマスか！」
lines.english: “Hello, my friend! What are you looking for?”

lines.japanese: 陽気な外人だ。髪も髭も眉毛も真っ黒で、やたらと彫りの深い顔。しかし俺は、プッシャーと呼ばれるこの手の商売人に用なんてない。生涯ない。
lines.english: A cheerful foreigner: pitch-black hair, beard, and eyebrows, all framing a sharply chiseled face. But I had no business with the kind of merchant known as a pusher. Not now. Not ever.

lines.japanese: 「赤いチャリンコ」
lines.english: “A red bicycle.”

lines.japanese: 俺はお呼びじゃないという風に片手を振って、ドスを利かせた声で答えた。
lines.english: I waved him off and answered in my most menacing growl.

lines.japanese: 「赤いチャリンコ？　オウ、赤いチャリンコないけど赤いユーロならあるヨ。青いドルフィン、緑スプリット、黄色ケンタウルス、他にも色々あるヨ」
lines.english: “Red bicycle? Oh, no red bicycle, but I have Red Euro. Blue Dolphin, Green Split, Yellow Centaurus—many other kinds.”

lines.japanese: 達者な日本語でおっさんは怪しげな営業を始めた。こっちは迷惑光線出しまくってるのに、くそっ、ジャパニーズ無愛想の通じないやつだ。
lines.english: The man launched into a shady sales pitch in fluent Japanese. I was firing every leave-me-alone ray I possessed, but damn it, he was immune to the sacred Japanese art of sullenness.

lines.japanese: 「いらないって。チャリンコしかいらないの俺」
lines.english: “I said I don't want any. A bicycle is the only thing I'm after.”

lines.japanese: 「チャリンコないけどチョコならあるヨ？　アイスもラムネも角砂糖もあるヨ？　受け渡しココじゃしませんから、ぜったい安全デス。チョト高いけど新製品もありマス。グロリアス、これ最高にバキバキよ」
lines.english: “No bicycle, but I have chocolate. Ice too, candy tablets, sugar cubes. We do not exchange here, so perfectly safe. New product too—little expensive. Glorious. Gets you completely wired.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺、チャリンコしかいらないから。ユーシー？　バイシコー。オンリー・レッドバイシコー」
lines.english: “No, listen, a bicycle is all I want. You see? Bicycle. Only red bicycle.”

lines.japanese: 「オーウ！　レッドバイシコゥ！？」
lines.english: “Oh! Red bicycle!?”

lines.japanese: おっさんは握りこぶしをふたつ前に付きだして、モモ上げ運動みたいに大きく足踏みした。ニカッと白い歯を覗かせて、大道芸人みたいにひょうきんな動き。
lines.english: The man thrust both fists before him and marched in place with high knees. White teeth flashed in a grin; he capered like a street performer.

lines.japanese: 相手の冷たい態度にもめげない国民性なんだろうか。俺はその笑顔につい引きこまれてしまった。
lines.english: Maybe his people simply didn't let a cold reception discourage them. Despite myself, his smile drew me in.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そう。赤い自転車。この辺で見たことない」
lines.english: “Yeah, that's it. A red bicycle. Ever seen one around here?”

lines.japanese: おっさんはワーオと叫んで両手を広げた。
lines.english: The man cried “Wow!” and threw his arms wide.

lines.japanese: 「見たヨ。さっき見たヨ」
lines.english: “I saw it. Just now, I saw it.”

lines.japanese: 馴れ馴れしく俺の肩を掴む。長袖から覗く手首から手の甲まで、黒い体毛がびっしり覆っていた。
lines.english: He clapped a familiar hand on my shoulder. Dense black hair covered every inch from the wrist showing beneath his sleeve to the back of his hand.

lines.japanese: 「……マジで」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 話が出来すぎててどうにも信用しにくかったけれど、俺はとりあえず冷めた声で続けた。
lines.english: It was much too convenient to trust, but for the moment I went on in a deliberately flat voice.

lines.japanese: 「え、どこで見たの」
lines.english: “Where'd you see it?”

lines.japanese: 「あッちノ……」
lines.english: “Over by...”

lines.japanese: しかし口を開こうとして、おっさんはいきなり両手で油っぽい黒髪を抱えこんでしまった。
lines.english: But just as he opened his mouth, the man suddenly clutched his greasy black hair in both hands.

lines.japanese: 「オーゥ、思いだせないヨ……頭が割れるようデス……」
lines.english: “Ohhh, I cannot remember... My head feels like it will split...”

lines.japanese: 外人特有のオーバージェスチャーでふるふると頭を振りながら、しかし、やつは腰の下からそろりそろりと右手を差しむけてきた。
lines.english: He shook his head with the broad, theatrical gestures foreigners always seemed to use. Meanwhile, his right hand crept slowly toward me from below his waist.

lines.japanese: 上を向いた浅黒いてのひらが何かを要求している。万国共通の分かりやすさだった。
lines.english: His brown hand lay palm-up, asking for something. Some forms of communication really were universal.

lines.japanese: 「へえー。うっそ、頭痛いの。やばいじゃん、ちょっとお巡りさん呼んできてやろうか」
lines.english: “Wow. Really? Your head hurts? That's bad. Want me to fetch a police officer?”

lines.japanese: 言いかえしてやると、外国人プッシャーは目を見開いて大きく息を吸いこんだ。
lines.english: At my reply, the foreign pusher's eyes flew open and he sucked in a tremendous breath.

lines.japanese: 「信じられマセン！　ニッポン人ひどいデス！」
lines.english: “I cannot believe! Japanese people are terrible!”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ。ジャパニーズ武士道っつんだよコレ。昔も今もサムライは曲がったことが大嫌いなんだよ。てめ、俺に贈賄行為を要求する気なら、セットで入国管理局まで付けてポリ呼んじゃうぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up. This is bushido, Japanese style. Samurai have always hated crooked dealing. If you’re asking me for a bribe, asshole, I’ll call the cops and Immigration both.”

lines.japanese: 俺は明日の日本を背負ったにわか外交官として、我が国のノーと言えないナショナルイメージを払拭せんばかりに強く言いはなった。
lines.english: As an impromptu diplomat carrying tomorrow's Japan on his shoulders, I delivered my declaration with enough force to obliterate our national reputation for never saying no.

lines.japanese: すると、先方は唐突にぽんと手を打った。
lines.english: At that, my foreign counterpart suddenly clapped his hands.

lines.japanese: 「ワオ！　思いだしたデス、レッド・バイシコー。ぴんふストリートの『ドンボルガン』前で見たデスよ」
lines.english: “Wow! I remember now, red bicycle. I saw it outside Don Volgan on Pinfu Street.”

lines.japanese: ああ、あの、なんか小じゃれてて高そうな食い物屋か。しかし出来すぎた話だ。
lines.english: Oh, that slightly fancy-looking place with the expensive air. Still, this story was much too convenient.

lines.japanese: 「本当かあ？」
lines.english: “You sure?”

lines.japanese: 「本当ヨ、信じてヨ！　だから警察に内緒デス。この辺りようやく常連さん増えてきタ、もう場所変えたくないのデス」
lines.english: “It is true, believe me! So you say nothing to police. Finally I have more regular customers here. I do not want to move again.”

lines.japanese: 「分かったよ。じゃあ信じるから。あーほら、センキューセンキュー」
lines.english: “All right. I'll believe you. Here—thank you, thank you.”

lines.japanese: 俺はおっさんの手を取って、わりと適当に国際交流を温めあった。
lines.english: I took the man’s hand, and we warmed international relations with a perfunctory shake.

lines.japanese: 手を放すと、やつは恨めしそうな目で俺を見つめながら嘆息した。
lines.english: When I let go, he gazed at me reproachfully and sighed.

lines.japanese: 「はあ、ニポン人かわいそデス。ひと握りの不心得者のために、国民みなが良識を疑われてしまう」
lines.english: “Ah, poor Japanese people. Because of small handful of bad citizens, good sense of entire nation comes under suspicion.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、おまえが言うなよ」
lines.english: “You're the last person who gets to say that.”

lines.japanese: 俺は最初のゲーセンに戻り、タバコの自販機に背中を預けて相棒を待った。
lines.english: I returned to the arcade, leaned against a cigarette machine, and waited for my partner.

lines.japanese: あ、いや、相棒ってもべつに深い意味はねーぞ。事件を追う刑事が同僚を指して言うときとかの、そういう「相棒」だからな。
lines.english: Ah, no. By *partner*, I didn’t mean anything deep. I meant it the way a detective uses the word for the colleague beside him on a case.

lines.japanese: ……まあ、べつに言いわけすることでもねえか。どうせおまえにはバレちゃうんだもんな、俺の気持ちとかそんなん。
lines.english: ...Not that I had anything to explain. You’d see straight through me anyway, wouldn’t you? My feelings and all that.

lines.japanese: にしても遅ぇな。俺がここに着いたとき、その時点ですでに約束の五分は過ぎてたんだけど。
lines.english: Still, she was late. The promised five minutes had already passed when I got back.

lines.japanese: まさか……ひょっとして、あいつも妙な外国人に引っかかってんのか？
lines.english: Don't tell me… Had she been caught by some strange foreigner too?

lines.japanese: たしかにあの小娘のキョロキョロっぷりは挙動不審気味だ。むしろプッシャーよりタチの悪いやつが寄ってくるかもしれない。
lines.english: The little girl's constant gawking did make her look suspicious. She might attract somebody even worse than a drug pusher.

lines.japanese: そうだ。もう夜も更けてる。厄介な性癖を持ったやつらの下半身が漲っててもおかしくない時間だ。
lines.english: It was late at night, after all. The hour when the lower halves of people with uglier appetites might well be surging with energy.

lines.japanese: あの小娘は女としてのフェロモンはさっぱりだけど、少女としての愛敬みたいのはある。んじゃないかと推測する。一般論として。
lines.english: The little girl had precious little allure as a woman, but she did possess a certain girlish charm. Probably. Speaking in purely general terms.

lines.japanese: しかもあいつ、情けないぐらい隙だらけだ（とくに口元とか）。もし俺が人身売買のバイヤーだったら、たぶん真っ先にあいつを狙うと思う。思うじゃねえよバカ。なんだその例え。
lines.english: And she was pathetically defenseless—especially around the mouth. If I were some buyer in the human-trafficking trade, she'd probably be the first one I targeted. What the hell do you mean, *probably*, idiot? What kind of example was that?

lines.japanese: ──遠くに、救急車のサイレンが聞こえた。
lines.english: —An ambulance siren wailed in the distance.

lines.japanese: 不吉な音は遠ざかり、店の中から漏れてくる、でたらめに絡みあったプライズゲーム群の電子音が残った。
lines.english: The ominous sound receded. What remained was the chaotic tangle of electronic jingles leaking from the arcade's prize machines.

lines.japanese: 「どこ行ったんだよ、あいつ……」
lines.english: “Where the hell did she go...?”

lines.japanese: 「なになに、どうしたのよ成田チャン」
lines.english: “What's this? What's wrong, Narita, baby?”

lines.japanese: 口の中で小さくつぶやくと、なぜかそれに答える声があった。
lines.english: I'd muttered under my breath, yet for some reason a voice answered.
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 振りかえると、濃ゆい顔立ちのあんちゃんが立っていた。サムライ風にまとめたドレッド頭。唇の両側をめいっぱい吊りあげて、夢見るようにニタニタ笑っている。
lines.english: I turned to find a young man with strongly defined features. His dreadlocks were tied up like a samurai’s, and the corners of his mouth stretched to their limit in a dreamy grin.

lines.japanese: 「お？　な～に、そんな泣きそうな顔しちゃって～。もっと人生楽しまなきゃ～、一服いっちゃえよ～」
lines.english: “Hm? What's with that face? You look ready to cry. Gotta enjoy life more. Come on, have a smoke.”

lines.japanese: 「……いや、誰おまえ」
lines.english: “...Who the hell are you?”

lines.japanese: 「ボンボ！　ひっでえよ成田チャ～ン、もう俺だよ俺、ほらほらコレ～」
lines.english: “Damn! That’s cold, Narita, baby. It’s me—me! Here, look at this.”

lines.japanese: ドレッド頭はサイケな色合いの民族衣装っぽい服をまくって、インナーのＴシャツを俺に見せた。そこにプリントされていたのは、いつか見た燃えるニワトリ。
lines.english: The dreadlocked man lifted his psychedelic shirt, which vaguely resembled traditional dress, to show me the T-shirt underneath. Printed across it was the flaming chicken I’d seen before.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、鳳ンとこの……」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. You're with Otori's...”

lines.japanese: 「アイアム、柳木原フレイムバーズ加盟組織『リディム』の四代目、島袋浩ａｋａチケドン。ヤーマン成田チャン、一緒にジョイントぷり～ず？」
lines.english: “I am Hiro Shimabukuro, a.k.a. Chikedon, fourth-generation head of Riddim, an affiliate of the Yanagihara Flame Birds. Ya man, Narita, baby. Come smoke a joint with me?”

lines.japanese: やつは呂律のあやしい口調で自己紹介を終えると、怪しげな手巻き煙草を一本抜きだした。俺はそれを速やかに、かつ指紋を付けずに元の箱へ戻させた。
lines.english: Having completed the introduction in a suspiciously slurred voice, he produced a dubious hand-rolled cigarette. I promptly made him put it back in its box without ever touching it myself.

lines.japanese: 「いや、いま俺、そんなくだらねーのに付きあってる場合じゃねンだよ。おまえさ、この辺で鳳の妹──」
lines.english: “Look, I don't have time for this stupid crap. Have you seen Otori's little sister around—”

lines.japanese: 「くだらねえーえ？　くだらねえって言ったァ？　ぶはーっ！　成田チャ～ン、あんたまでそんな、政府の情報操作に洗脳されちゃってンのォ～！」
lines.english: “Stuuupid? Did you call it stupid? Bwah! Narita, baby, don't tell me even you've been brainwashed by government propaganda!”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　洗脳？　なんの話だ、そんなことよりおまえ、この辺で鳳の──」
lines.english: “Huh? Brainwashed? What are you talking about? More importantly, have you seen Otori's—”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことじゃねえよォ！　分かってんのォ、ほんとはコレ、酒とかタバコよりよっぽど安全なんだよォ！？　つか規制する方が頭おかしいんじゃ、ボゲがァ！」
lines.english: “Don't you ‘more importantly’ me! Don't you know this stuff's way safer than alcohol or tobacco? Banning it is what's crazy, dumbass!”

lines.japanese: 溜息が出そうになった。俺の知るかぎりハッパの愛好家はみな同じような高説を唱えたがる。学術的な真偽は知らないけど、少なくともこの国の法律が変わらないうちは俺にとってまるで興味の湧かないテーマだ。
lines.english: I nearly sighed. Every devotee of weed I’d ever met liked to preach the same sermon. I didn’t know whether it held up scientifically, but until the law in this country changed, I had zero interest in the subject.

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいから。いいからおまえ、往来でそんなもん高々と掲げてる時点で、おまえの方がはるかに頭おかしいから」
lines.english: “Enough. The fact you’re standing in the street waving that thing over your head already makes you way crazier than me.”

lines.japanese: 「成田チャンは考え方が島国だなあ。閉じてる閉じてる。ひとをおかしいと決めつける前にさ、まず自分の物差しを疑おうよ。もしかしたら国民全員、そろって物差しひん曲がってるかもしれないわけでしょォ～？」
lines.english: “Narita, baby, that's island-nation thinking. Closed, closed, closed. Before you declare somebody else crazy, question your own yardstick. Maybe the whole country is using the same bent ruler, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、待て。いま誰もそんな、マクロな視点の論議してねえよ」
lines.english: “Wait. Nobody was having some grand macro-level debate here.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱさあ、国会でボング焚いて、国の中枢から頭を柔らかくすべきなんだよ。ストレス・不景気・差別意識、みーんなＴＨＣがブッ飛ばしてくれンだから。成田チャンも試しにブリッと一服いっちゃおうよォ～」
lines.english: “What we ought to do is fire up a bong in the Diet and loosen the country up from its very center. Stress, recession, prejudice—THC will blow it all away. Come on, Narita, baby, take one fat hit and see.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、今それどこじゃねンだよ。おまえ、鳳の妹見なかった」
lines.english: “I told you, I don't have time for this. Have you seen Otori's little sister?”

lines.japanese: 淀みなく語りつづけるドレッド野郎の一瞬の隙をついて、ようやく俺は言葉を挿しはさんだ。予想外といか予想通りというか、やつはあっさりと頷いた。
lines.english: I finally caught a split-second gap in the dreadlocked bastard’s nonstop spiel and wedged my question into it. Unexpectedly—or perhaps exactly as expected—he nodded at once.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、鳴タロちゃんね～」
lines.english: “Oh, Narutaro? Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ、見たの。どこ。どこいた」
lines.english: “Seriously? You saw her? Where? Where was she?”

lines.japanese: 「それが、ぷくく、成田チャンも見てあげてよ～。あの子なら今あっちで、みんなにガンガンぶち込まれちゃって、もうヒィーヒィー言ってッからさぁ～！」
lines.english: “Pukuku. Narita, you gotta see this. They've been pounding it into her nonstop over there. Poor thing's practically screaming!”

lines.japanese: 「ああッ！？」
lines.english: “What!?”

lines.japanese: 「くっくっく、かーわいそォにねェ～、ぶひゃひゃひゃひゃ！」
lines.english: “Kukkukku. Aww, poor little thing. Buhyahyahyahya!”

lines.japanese: 「てめェ……このド外道がァ……」
lines.english: “You… You depraved piece of shit…”

lines.japanese: 「あたっ、あててて！　ちょ、な～に、なにマジギレしてんだよォ～！　あだだだ、ちょっと、はやく、鳴タロ助けて！」
lines.english: “Ow! Owowow! Hey, what—why're you seriously losing it, man? Owowow! Quick, Naru-boy, save me!”

lines.japanese: 「はいー？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「あー面白かったー」
lines.english: “Oh, that was fun.”

lines.japanese: 「あー！　隼人さん遅ーい、遅刻ですよ、もおー」
lines.english: “Oh! Hayato, you're laaate. Honestly, you're late!”

lines.japanese: 「……え、おまえ何してたの」
lines.english: “…What were you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「何してたじゃないですよー。隼人さんが来ないから、ここにいた皆さんが遊んでくれてたんですよー」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what was I doing? You didn't come, so everyone here played with me while I waited.”

lines.japanese: 鳴に続いて、店の中の階段をぞろぞろ下りてくる見覚えのある集団がいた。先頭が抱えてるプラスチックのでかいカップに、小さな銀貨がたっぷり詰まっていた。
lines.english: Behind Naru came a familiar crowd, filing down the stairs from inside the arcade. The person in front carried a huge plastic cup brimming with little silver tokens.

lines.japanese: 「あー……ああ、スロット？」
lines.english: “Oh… Oh. The slots?”

lines.japanese: 「そーなんですよー。もー私行かなきゃってひーひー言ってるのに、皆さん遠慮すんなってがんがんメダル入れちゃうんですもーん」
lines.english: “Exactly. I kept telling them I had to go, practically crying over it, but they said not to be shy and kept pouring in more and more tokens.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ああ、そう……へえ、良かったな」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. I see… Huh. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: 「ったくよー、成田チャンもキャパ小さいよねえ？　ほんのちょっと借りただけじゃ～ん。もっとラブ＆ピースの精神でさァ、つまんないヤキモチとか勘弁してよォ～」
lines.english: “Come on, Narita, don't be so uptight. We only borrowed her for a little while. Get in the love & peace spirit and can the petty jealousy, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「やきもちっ！？」
lines.english: “Jealousy!?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、そーゆーんじゃなくて」
lines.english: “No, it wasn't like that.”

lines.japanese: 「そーゆーんじゃなくて、じゃねーだろォ！　いッきなり、ひとの襟首掴んでよー。あんたマジ、えれーカオしてたぜえ？」
lines.english: “Don't give me that! You grabbed me by the collar out of nowhere. Man, you should've seen your face.”

lines.japanese: 「く、詳しく！」
lines.english: “D-details, please!”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ、違げんだよ、ちょっとした日本語のすれ違いなんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. You've got it wrong. It was a minor linguistic misunderstanding.”

lines.japanese: 「は～あ、しょーがねえなあ。じゃー、まー、そーゆーことにしといてやるけどさァ、ぶふふ？」
lines.english: “Haaah... Fine. If that's your story, I'll let you have it. Heh heh?”

lines.japanese: 「うふふ？」
lines.english: “Heh heh?”

lines.japanese: 「んだコラ、見下ろしてんじゃねえよてめえら。嘲笑するな。俺を嘲笑するな」
lines.english: “What are you two looking down on me for? Don't sneer. Stop sneering at me.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに。じゃあ、あいつらも、おまえのチャリ探しの最中だったの」
lines.english: “Wait. So were those guys looking for your bike too?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、はいー、そうらしいんですよー。もー、なんで私が自転車盗まれたこと知ってるんですかねー」
lines.english: “Yes, apparently. Though I do wonder how they knew my bicycle had been stolen.”

lines.japanese: うん、それはね、ぼくがうっかり森里くんに話しちゃったからだと思う。
lines.english: Well, you see, little old me may have accidentally told Morisato.

lines.japanese: 「あー、でもそういえば私、前にぽろりと話しちゃったかもしれません」
lines.english: “Oh—but come to think of it, perhaps I let it slip to them before.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それだろ、間違いねーよ。いや、それだって絶対。間違いねーよ。まず間違いねーよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, that’s it. No question. Definitely. Absolutely. No doubt about it.”

lines.japanese: 俺は怒涛の間違いねーよ攻撃で、やつをむりやり納得させた。
lines.english: I steamrolled her into agreement with a relentless barrage of “no doubt about it.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でもさ。あいつらがあのゲーセンにいたのはなんでよ」
lines.english: “But wait. Why were they at that arcade?”

lines.japanese: 「たまたま遊びに来ただけなのか、それとも俺らみたいにＲ－ウィングから情報を引きだしたのか……」
lines.english: “Did they just happen to come for fun, or did they get the lead from R-Wing the way we did...?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、どうなんですかねー。それは聞かなかったですけどー、ただＲなんたらの方々も同じものを探していることは、皆さんご存知でしたねー」
lines.english: “I wonder. I didn't ask, but everyone did know that the R-something people were searching for the same thing.”

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか。あいつら、いま形だけは同じチームだから、そういう情報は共有してるのかもしれない。
lines.english: Oh, right. Technically, they all belonged to the same team now. Maybe they shared that kind of information.

lines.japanese: 「あいつらにはぜってー負けねーと、ちょっぴり引いてる私の前で鼻息荒く語っておられましたよー」
lines.english: “They stood there breathing fire about how they’d never lose to those people. I was backing away a little at the time.”

lines.japanese: 「……ああ、そう」
lines.english: “...Right. I see.”

lines.japanese: どこまでも負けず嫌いなやつらだ。
lines.english: Competitive to the bitter end, every last one of them.

lines.japanese: まあ、殴り合いド突き合いじゃないし、勝手に好きなだけ張りあってろっつー感じだけど。
lines.english: At least they weren’t trading punches and kicks. They could compete to their hearts’ content for all I cared.

lines.japanese: 「そういう意味じゃアレだよな。おまえがチャリンコ盗まれたおかげで、こう、何十人もの若者が健全な生き甲斐を見つけたっつーわけだよな」
lines.english: “Look at it this way. Thanks to your bike getting stolen, dozens of young people have found a wholesome purpose in life.”

lines.japanese: 「や、すげえなおい。おまえの抜けっぷりが、世のため人のためになったわけじゃん。おまえソレ、いつか世界を救うんじゃねーの。かっけーよマジ、おまえさ、もっとなんか盗まれろよ」
lines.english: “That's incredible. Your absentmindedness has finally served the greater good. At this rate, you might save the world someday. Seriously, amazing. You ought to get more stuff stolen.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、よく分からないですけど、なんか誉められてるみたいなんで喜んでおきますね。わあい」
lines.english: “I don't quite understand, but you seem to be praising me, so I shall be pleased. Hooray.”

lines.japanese: 「あんさ。そんでさ。俺、新しい目撃情報入ったんだけど」
lines.english: “Hey, anyway—I got a new sighting.”

lines.japanese: 「あらまあ、こちらにも入りましたよー」
lines.english: “My goodness. So did we.”

lines.japanese: 「は。マジかよ。ああ、あのジャンキー軍団から聞いたんだ」
lines.english: “What, seriously? From that army of junkies?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー。数日前、北口のモンキホウーテ付近に赤い背もたれ付きの自転車が停まっていたそうでー」
lines.english: “Yes. Apparently a red bicycle with a backrest was parked near Monki Hoote by the north exit a few days ago.”

lines.japanese: 「俺が引いた方の情報は、あんま信用できるネタ元じゃねーんだよな……一応言っとくと、目撃場所はあそこ、ほらピンフ通りの、ドンなんとか言うしゃらくさいレストラン」
lines.english: “The lead I got isn’t from the most trustworthy source... but for what it’s worth, the sighting was outside that pretentious restaurant on Pinfu Street. Don Something.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい、ドンボルガンですか。たしかスペイン料理の」
lines.english: “Ah, yes. Don Volgan, perhaps? The Spanish restaurant.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに、スペイン料理って。闘牛とか食うの」
lines.english: “What is Spanish food? Do they eat bullfighting bulls or something?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、スペインたしか国内でも地域によって食文化違うんですけどー、ひとことで申しますと闘牛は食べません」
lines.english: “Well, food culture in Spain varies by region, but to put it briefly, they do not eat fighting bulls.”

lines.japanese: 「んだよ、つまんねえなあ。俄然やる気なくなんなドンボルガン」
lines.english: “What the hell? That's boring. There goes every last scrap of interest I had in Don Volgan.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、じゃー、モンキホウーテ行ってみますー？」
lines.english: “Then shall we try Monki Hoote?”

lines.japanese: 「だ、な……んー、おし、そうすっか……」
lines.english: “Yeah... Mm. All right. Let's do that.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは駅前のスクランブル交差点を渡って、次の調査場所へ向かった。
lines.english: We crossed the scramble crossing in front of the station and headed for the next search site.

lines.japanese: 「あとおまえソレ、『ウ』はいらないから」
lines.english: “And drop the extra ‘o.’”
